meta.titre: The Annunciation and Infancy of Jesus: Gabriel's messages, the Holy Spirit and the songs of Luke
meta.sous_theme: Annunciations to Zechariah, Mary and Joseph; the Holy Spirit; hymns and prayers in the infancy narratives
tags: A Level Religious Studies - annunciation and infancy of jesus

source.epreuve_titre: GCE A/L Religious Studies past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: Every December, churches in Cameroon, from Douala to Bamenda, fill with carols, children dressed as shepherds and a girl playing Mary. The Gospel of Luke even gives us songs that Christians still sing: Mary's praise of God and Zechariah's blessing. At A Level, examiners expect more than the Christmas story. They ask what is special about the announcement of Jesus' birth, what part the Holy Spirit plays and what the hymns and prayers express.

items: Christians believe that Jesus of Nazareth is the Son of God and the Saviour, and the Gospels of Matthew and Luke tell of his birth and childhood.
Luke is addressed to a reader named Theophilus and gives much space to the Holy Spirit, prayer, joy and the humble people of society.
In the Old Testament, God sometimes announced the birth of a child to a woman who was childless, for example to Sarah, the wife of Abraham.

sections.titre: The infancy narratives: the annunciations, the Holy Spirit and the songs
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The annunciations
| Annunciation | Recipient and setting | Main message | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| Birth of John the Baptist (Luke 1) | Zechariah, an elderly priest, serving in the temple at Jerusalem. His wife Elizabeth was unable to have children. | The child will be called John, will be filled with the Holy Spirit even before birth and will prepare people for the Lord. | Zechariah doubts and asks for proof; he is unable to speak until the child is born. |
| Birth of Jesus (Luke 1) | Mary, a young woman engaged to Joseph of the house of David, at Nazareth in Galilee. | She will conceive and bear a son named Jesus, who will be called Son of the Most High, will receive the throne of David and will reign for ever. The Holy Spirit will come upon her. | Mary asks how this can be, then accepts: she calls herself the servant of the Lord. |
| Birth of Jesus (Matthew 1) | Joseph, in a dream, troubled that Mary is expecting a child. | The child is from the Holy Spirit; he is to be named Jesus because he will save his people from their sins. | Joseph obeys and takes Mary to be his wife. |

Luke tells the annunciation to Mary and Matthew tells the one to Joseph. Do not mix the two Gospels.

### What is unique in the announcement to Mary
Christians point to several features: the child is conceived through the Holy Spirit without a human father; he is declared Son of the Most High and heir of David's kingdom; the message comes to a young woman of no rank in a small town; and Mary is invited to take part freely through her answer.

### The Holy Spirit in the infancy narratives
In Luke the Spirit is at work throughout: John is to be filled from birth, Elizabeth and Zechariah are filled and speak in praise, the Spirit comes upon Mary, and the Spirit rests upon Simeon, who is told that he will see the Lord's Messiah. The Spirit makes the birth possible, inspires prophecy and guides people to recognise who Jesus is.

### Hymns and prayers
Luke includes songs: Mary's Magnificat, Zechariah's Benedictus, the angels' praise at the birth of Jesus and Simeon's prayer in the temple. Their themes are joy, praise of God, peace, the keeping of God's promises, the lifting of the humble and salvation open to all peoples. Yet joy is not the only note: Simeon warns Mary that she will suffer, so the narratives look forward to the cross as well.

variantes.nom: Question on the hymns and prayers
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a statement about joy, peace or praise in the infancy narratives is given for comment.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name each song and its speaker, give the occasion, explain two or three themes, and judge the statement: joy and peace are strong themes, but Simeon's warning and the threat to the child in Matthew show that the narratives also contain sorrow.

variantes.nom: Question on the Holy Spirit's role
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to discuss the place of the Holy Spirit in the birth stories.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Collect examples in order: John, Elizabeth, Zechariah, Mary, Simeon. For each state what the Spirit does (fills, empowers to praise, overshadows, reveals). Then judge whether the Spirit 'takes precedence' or shares the stage with other themes such as fulfilment of promises, the Davidic kingship and the humility of the people.

sections.enonce_markdown: Compare the announcement of the birth of John the Baptist with the announcement of the birth of Jesus in Luke chapter 1. (25 marks)

etapes.justification: 'Compare' means give similarities and differences, with evidence for each.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Both accounts must be treated side by side.

etapes.justification: A two-column mind or a plan in two paragraphs keeps the comparison clear.
Facts from the text show knowledge.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Both announcements are made by the angel Gabriel; in both the recipient is afraid and is told not to be afraid; in both the angel gives the child's name; both children are to be great in God's plan; the Holy Spirit is linked to both.

etapes.justification: Differences show the uniqueness of each account.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Zechariah, a priest, is told in the temple at Jerusalem, while Mary is told at Nazareth. Zechariah's wife is elderly and unable to have children, whereas Mary is a young woman engaged to be married. Zechariah doubts and is left unable to speak; Mary asks how and then accepts. John is to prepare the way for the Lord, while Jesus is called Son of the Most High and will reign on David's throne.

etapes.justification: The conclusion shows what the comparison means.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The two stories are parallel in form, but Luke makes the second greater than the first, presenting Jesus as the one for whom John prepares.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer, in brief. Both announcements come from Gabriel, include the words 'do not be afraid', give the child a name and promise a great role, and involve the Holy Spirit. They differ in the recipient (a priest in the temple against a young woman in Nazareth), in the circumstances (an elderly couple unable to have children against a virgin engaged to Joseph), in the response (Zechariah's doubt and loss of speech against Mary's question and acceptance) and in the child's role (forerunner against Son of the Most High and king). Luke thereby shows that John prepares the way and Jesus is the greater.

items.erreur_markdown: Placing the shepherds and the angels' song in Matthew, and the visit of the wise men in Luke.
items.pourquoi_faux: The shepherds belong to Luke; the visit of the wise men from the east belongs to Matthew. Mixing the Gospels is a factual error.
items.correction_markdown: 'In Luke, shepherds are told by angels; in Matthew, wise men from the east come with gifts.'

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that Gabriel announced the birth of Jesus to Joseph.
items.pourquoi_faux: In Luke the angel Gabriel speaks to Mary. In Matthew, an angel of the Lord speaks to Joseph in a dream.
items.correction_markdown: Name the correct person and Gospel for each annunciation.

items.erreur_markdown: Retelling the whole Christmas story instead of answering a 'discuss' or 'comment' question.
items.pourquoi_faux: A narrative does not weigh a statement. The examiner wants arguments and judgement.
items.correction_markdown: Pick relevant episodes only and link each to the statement in the question.

items.erreur_markdown: Stating that Mary doubted God's message in the same way as Zechariah.
items.pourquoi_faux: Luke presents Zechariah's reply as doubt followed by a sign of silence. Mary's question 'how can this be?' is followed by acceptance.
items.correction_markdown: Contrast the two responses and use them as evidence of Mary's faith.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that the Holy Spirit appears only at Mary's annunciation.
items.pourquoi_faux: In Luke the Spirit is mentioned in connection with John, Elizabeth, Zechariah, Mary and Simeon.
items.correction_markdown: List several figures and say what the Spirit does for each.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the person to whom Gabriel appeared in the temple and the town where Gabriel appeared to Mary.
items.solution_markdown: Gabriel appeared to Zechariah, the priest, in the temple, and to Mary in Nazareth in Galilee. **Zechariah; Nazareth.**

items.enonce_markdown: Explain how the Holy Spirit is shown at work in the lives of Elizabeth, Zechariah and Mary in Luke's infancy narrative.
items.solution_markdown: Model points. Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit when Mary visits and recognises Mary as the mother of her Lord. Zechariah is filled with the Spirit when his speech returns and he praises God and prophesies about his son. The Holy Spirit comes upon Mary, who is told that she will bear a child in a special way. In each case the Spirit inspires recognition of Jesus and praise of God. **Award a mark for each correct person with an accurate description of the Spirit's action, up to the total marks.**

items.enonce_markdown: 'The infancy narratives show that the good news is first of all for the poor and humble.' Discuss with examples from Luke.
items.solution_markdown: Plan. For: the angels' message goes to shepherds; Mary is a young woman of no rank; her song speaks of the lowly being lifted up and the hungry filled; the offering at the presentation in the temple is two young birds, a modest gift; Simeon and Anna are faithful, ordinary people in the temple. Against or qualifications: Luke also names rulers and links Jesus to David's royal line; in Matthew wise men bring costly gifts; the message is finally for all peoples. **Conclusion: the poor and humble have a special place, but Luke also presents salvation as universal.**

items_markdown: Luke 1 and 2 give the annunciations to Zechariah and Mary, and Matthew 1 gives the one to Joseph; do not mix the Gospels.
The announcement to Mary is unique because the child is conceived through the Holy Spirit and declared Son of the Most High and heir to David's throne.
The Holy Spirit fills John, Elizabeth, Zechariah and Simeon and comes upon Mary: he inspires praise and recognition of Jesus.
The Magnificat, the Benedictus, the angels' praise and Simeon's prayer express joy, peace, thanksgiving and God's faithfulness, but Simeon also warns of suffering.
For 'comment', 'discuss' or 'examine', give evidence, explanation and a judgement, not a retelling.
